table_title: For each of the four largest world religions (Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism), list five major holy or pilgrimage sites with their city, country, and a brief note on why each site is significant.
db_analog: SELECT religion, list_position, site, city, country, significance_note FROM holy_sites_selection WHERE religion IN ('Christianity','Islam','Hinduism','Buddhism') ORDER BY religion, list_position
temporal_note: Wikipedia articles accessed 2026-04-28. The four-religion universe is anchored to the largest groups in Wikipedia 'Major religious groups' (Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism); folk religions and 'unaffiliated' are excluded as they are not coherent traditions with shared holy-site lists. Per-religion site selections are anchored to that religion's primary Wikipedia pilgrimage / holy-sites article and corroborated against per-site Wikipedia articles for Islam (cycle-1 audit fix: the consolidated 'Holiest sites in Islam' article was flagged with a Wikipedia LLM-generated-content warning in November 2025 and was replaced with five per-site Wikipedia articles for the Islam rows). Site selections are stable historical traditions and are not expected to drift on a multi-year timescale, but the article snapshots on which the selections rely may be edited. The 'Significance Note' column is a one-sentence paraphrase of the cited article's description of why the site is significant; cell-level evaluation should treat semantic similarity to the article phrasing as success rather than exact-string match. The 'List Position' column is a within-religion ordinal (1 through 5) that records the order in which sites are listed in the cited per-religion source; it is a non-key column (cycle-2 PK is (Religion, Site)) and should not be interpreted as an absolute holiness ranking — see the cycle-1 / cycle-2 audit responses for the reframing from 'top 5 holiest ranked' to 'five major sites selected' and the PK change.
_extraction_notes: Universe (4 religions): drawn from Wikipedia 'Major religious groups' largest-groups table — Christianity (~2.3B), Islam (~2.0B), Hinduism (~1.2B), Buddhism (~0.3B). Folk religions (~0.2B) and 'unaffiliated' (~24% of population) are excluded as the former is heterogeneous (no unified holy-site list) and the latter is not a religion. Per-religion selection convention (cycle-1 audit reframe — was 'top 5 ranked holiest', now 'five major holy or pilgrimage sites'): Christianity follows the 'three great pilgrimages of Christendom' (Jerusalem, Rome, Santiago) named by Pope Alexander VI plus Lourdes and Jasna Góra as the most-emphasized modern Catholic pilgrimage centers per the 'Christian pilgrimage' article; Islam selects the universally cited top-3 (Mecca, Medina, Jerusalem — confirmed individually by per-site Wikipedia articles as 'most significant', 'second holiest', 'third holiest') plus Hebron's Cave of the Patriarchs (per the article: 'according to some sources, the mosque is the 4th holiest in Islam' — note the article qualifies this with 'other sources rank other sites as 4th') plus Imam Ali Shrine in Najaf (per the article: 'the fourth holiest Islamic site' for Shia Muslims); Hinduism uses the Sapta Puri (seven holy cities) tradition documented in the Wikipedia 'Sapta Puri' article and takes the first 5 in the article's canonical order (Ayodhya, Mathura, Haridwar, Varanasi, Kanchipuram); Buddhism uses the Four Holy Sites identified by the Buddha in the Mahaparinibbana Sutta (Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Kushinagar) plus Rajgir as the most prominent supplementary 'Eight Great Places' site per the 'Buddhist pilgrimage sites' article. Schema: (Religion, Site) is the composite PK (cycle-2 audit fix; was (Religion, List Position) in cycles 0-1) because List Position is a curator-listed display ordinal and is not a consistently source-defined ranking — making it a non-key column rather than part of the PK keeps the table honest about the selected-not-ranked semantics. List Position is retained as a non-key 1-5 ordinal that records the order in which sites are listed in the cited per-religion source for ease of reading; it should not be interpreted as an absolute holiness rank. The 'Significance Note' column is a one-sentence paraphrase of the cited article's significance description and should be evaluated by semantic similarity rather than exact-string match. Result: 4 religions x 5 sites = 20 rows x 6 columns, 0 duplicate composite PKs. The country column ranges over 10 distinct countries (Saudi Arabia, Israel, Palestine, Iraq, Vatican City, Spain, France, Poland, India, Nepal); Old City Jerusalem sites (Holy Sepulchre, Al-Aqsa) are listed as Israel because Israel administers the Old City de facto; West Bank sites (Hebron) are listed as Palestine following Wikipedia convention. Cycle-1 audit notes: (a) data row count and the 4-religion universe are unchanged; (b) Hinduism rows were re-ordered to match the Sapta Puri article's canonical first-5 order (Ayodhya at position 1, Varanasi at position 4) — the previous staged order had Varanasi at position 1; (c) Islam consolidated source 'Holiest sites in Islam' was replaced with 5 per-site Wikipedia articles because the consolidated article carries a Wikipedia LLM-generated-content warning (Nov 2025); (d) Hindu pilgrimage sites consolidated source was replaced with 'Sapta Puri' as a more direct universe + ordering anchor.
